edges.effect_quant: Tart-cherry supplementation does not erase muscle damage, but it does appear to reduce post-exercise soreness and help functional recovery over the following days.
edges.population: physically active adults and athletes after strenuous exercise
edges.mechanism: Tart cherries are rich in anthocyanins and other polyphenols that may blunt post-exercise inflammatory signaling and oxidative stress, reducing the symptom burden that follows heavy eccentric or repeated-sprint work. The effect appears stronger on soreness and functional recovery than on classic damage markers like creatine kinase.
edges.summary: The strongest evidence says tart cherry helps recovery more than it helps performance on the day itself. Meta-analysis and placebo-controlled trials show a modest but repeatable reduction in delayed soreness and somewhat faster return of strength or jump performance after strenuous exercise.
edges.caveats: The literature is heterogeneous in exercise protocol, formulation, and dosing schedule. Benefits are usually modest, and biomarker effects are less consistent than patient-relevant recovery outcomes.

evidence.citation: Brown M et al 2021 Int J Sport Nutr Exerc Metab
evidence.notes: Tart Cherry Supplementation and Recovery From Strenuous Exercise: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.

effect_quant.comparator: muscle soreness after tart cherry versus placebo

evidence.notes: The Effects of Montmorency Tart Cherry Concentrate Supplementation on Recovery Following Prolonged, Intermittent Exercise.

evidence.citation: Lanham-New SA et al 2019 Eur J Sport Sci
evidence.notes: Montmorency tart cherry (Prunus cerasus L.) supplementation accelerates recovery from exercise-induced muscle damage in females.
